title: Canonical hybrid plurisubharmonic extension of logarithmic-growth metrics and the continuous converse after shrinking
difficulty_reason: After BBJ/Reboulet non-Archimedean limits, classical Demailly/BE regularization, rational convex approximation, relative global generation and vanishing, DPS local comparisons and Ohsawa-Takegoshi are treated as inputs, the authored burden is to use one multiplier-ideal Hilbert basis to produce complex square sums and non-Archimedean maxima, control finite truncations including analytic singularities on both sides, and pass a compatible regularization to the hybrid limit. Appendix A.3, convex transfer and continuous sufficiency support this one H2; none earns another count or an H3.

exact_primary_comparisons.title: Modulus of continuity of Monge--Amp\`ere potentials in big cohomology classes
exact_primary_comparisons.statement:
\begin{lemma}\label{lem extend GZ12 prop 5.3} Under the assumption of Lemma \ref{lem sup<cap}, assume further that $v_2\geq u$. We have
the following
	inequality 
$$\sup_{X } (v_1-u)\leq \left(2+\dfrac{2 M C^{1/n}}{\lambda^{1+\alpha}(1-2^{-\alpha})}\right)\|(v_1-u)_+\|_{L^1(\nu)}^{\frac{\alpha}{(n+1)\alpha+n}},$$
where $\nu=\mathbf{1}_{\{u<v_1\}}\theta_u^n$ and $(v_1-u)_+=\max(v_1-u,0)$.
\end{lemma}
exact_primary_comparisons.owner_comparison: Actual lemma5.3 is an L1-to-sup potential comparison under its named capacity premise; it is an input-type inequality rather than any of the four selected primary claims.

exact_primary_comparisons.title: Unramified-extension convergence of normalized pluricanonical measures to weighted Shilov atoms for smooth proper varieties over non-archimedean local fields
exact_primary_comparisons.statement:
\begin{theorem}\label{thm:shi}
As~$K'$ ranges through $\mathcal{E}^{\ur}_K$, the measures $\nu_{\form,K'}$ converge to the discrete measure
\[
\mu_{X,\form}=\sum_{x\in \Sh(X,\form)}\tdeg_{K}(x)\delta_x
\]
on $X^{\an}$, where $\tdeg_K$ is the tame degree function from Section \ref{ss:tamedeg}, and $\Sh(X,\form)$ is the Shilov boundary of $(X,\form)$ defined in Section \ref{sec:shilov}.
\end{theorem}

exact_primary_comparisons.title: On the pluricomplex Poisson kernel and the associated complex Monge--Amp\`{e}re equation
exact_primary_comparisons.statement:
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:unique-maximizer} For every $\lambda\in(0,\, 1)$ and $(x,\, y)\in D$, the supremum defining $f_{\lambda}(x,\,y)$ is attained at a unique point $t=t_{\lambda}(x,\,y)$. Moreover, this maximizer depends smoothly on $(x,\, y)$  so that $f_{\lambda}$ is
smooth, with
   $$
   {\rm grad}\, f_{\lambda}=c_{\lambda}\circ t_{\lambda} \bigl(e^{t_{\lambda}},\, -1\bigr)
   \qquad {\rm and } \qquad  \rank {\rm Hess}_{\mathbb R}f_{\lambda}\equiv 1.
   $$
\end{lemma}
exact_primary_comparisons.owner_comparison: Actual lem:unique-maximizer controls the unique maximizing parameter f_lambda and a rank-one Hessian; it is not a finite-energy family metric or hybrid isometric realization.

cross_current_new_core_comparison.burden: Use the same multiplier-ideal Hilbert basis for complex square sums and NA maxima, compatible finite truncation and singularity regularization at the hybrid limit.
Global integer-section realization on M(Z), including forced Archimedean shadows, summable outgoing slopes and synchronization of opposite monotonicity.
Relative Perron, zero-curvature energy pairing, rooftop and subharmonic distance comparisons with fixed smooth boundary, giving a Lelong-slope metric and completeness.
Two-boundary model-net lift with energy-Lelong locking and annular-rooftop/NA-rooftop identification yielding the hybrid maximal isometric image.

literal_source_observations.observation: phi_(m,m0) is already defined with denominator 2(m+m0) at 1254, while 1289 writes an additional (m+m0)^(-1) before phi_(m,m0) in its decreasing-limit sentence. Preserve the source expressions; do not silently normalize one to the other.

The two continuous maps and density argument are formulated on CPSH, while the final 1312 sentence says they coincide on PSH. Keep this literal tail sentence as metadata; the selected theorem converse remains restricted to CPSH and shrinking.

The theorem states singularities of I_(2^j), while its final sequence uses phi_(2^j-m0,m0) and 1705 identifies phi_(m,m0) singularities with I_m. Preserve all three source statements and their relation; do not replace the specified ideal or manufacture the missing index reconciliation.
n is set to dim Y at 1674; the Hilbert norm uses omega^n at 1692, while later local estimates use omega^(n+1). Record the literal exponents without changing a dimension convention or proof.
The appendix writes Y triple-prime at 1710 and Y double-prime at 1769, while surrounding subsets are Y-prime, Y_c and Y_(c-prime). Keep as original subset-name observations; do not invent subsets.

The projective-space example writes a logarithm of a squared sum at 1053 and a maximum of absolute values without a log at 1058. Retain those literal expressions alongside the actual definitions and later lemma; do not rewrite them.

The model is described as a model of itself at 342 (the raw note incorrectly points to 340); 706 writes mathscr X(x) in a sentence otherwise using H(x). These are literal symbol observations, not missing proof material.

The introduction uses pluripolar while the later discussion explicitly uses non-pluripolar for the special point. Preserve both original locations; do not resolve their terminology by rewriting the text.

normal_observations_not_author_gaps.reason: The reciprocal powers convert function values and norms between opposite rescaling directions. The explicit loose phi_t identity states the fibers involved; this is a normalization convention, not a gap inferred merely from reciprocals. The 949 raw note duplicates 948.

Normalized ord_E and negative-log absolute-value conventions have different scale factors. Preserve the quoted factors when assembling; a scale comparison alone is not proof of a defect or absent author material.

Maxima of log norms and minima of vanishing orders are linked by the valuation/sign convention. A raw min-versus-max difference alone is not a source gap; retain the exact generic-Lelong/model-metric formulas as needed context without independently certifying their equality.
R/disk base labels and placement of the relative-base subscript must be retained literally. They do not indicate a missing canonical-model construction.
Delimiter sizing and the unmatched display parenthesis are typography observations; they do not remove the specified maps or their author proof.
A shortened phi symbol in an explanatory paragraph is not by itself an author-proof omission.
Hybrid coefficient norm and absorption of rational constants into pure FS metrics are intentional definitions/constructions, not defects.
The discontinuous special-point example is an intentional scope boundary; unnamed diagram arrows are ordinary layout. Neither should be presented as missing author content.
